name: Cefaclor
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 250 mg every 8 hours; doubled for more severe infections (such as pneumonia) or less susceptible organisms

key_interactions.effect: Increased anticoagulant effect reported, rarely with bleeding (label).

key_interactions.action: Expect higher cefaclor levels; monitor for adverse effects.

key_interactions.effect: Reduce absorption of extended-release cefaclor tablets when taken within 1 hour of the dose; H2 blockers do not (extended-release label).
key_interactions.action: Separate the antacid from an extended-release tablet by at least 1 hour.

key_interactions.effect: Antibiotics may act on the vaccine strain and prevent a protective immune response (Vivotif label).
key_interactions.action: Do not give the vaccine during cefaclor treatment.

key_interactions.effect: Antimicrobial therapy may interfere with the effectiveness of BCG (TICE BCG label).
key_interactions.action: Postpone BCG instillations during cefaclor treatment.

key_interactions.effect: Contains bacterial spores; antibacterials should not be given at the same time (Vowst label).
key_interactions.action: Finish cefaclor before starting Vowst; its label completes antibacterial treatment 2 to 4 days before the first dose.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Urine glucose tests (copper reduction: Benedict's, Fehling's, Clinitest)

pk.half_life_eskd: 2.3 to 2.8 hours with no kidney function (label)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 60% to 85% unchanged in urine within 8 hours

revision_log.change: Interactions added from a US cefaclor label (Hikma, 2020): oral anticoagulants (increased effect), probenecid (reduced renal excretion), false-positive copper-reduction urine glucose.
Batch 6 summary approved by Dr. Rivero with the pharmacology review corrections.

Interactions re-sourced to the pinned Azorian label (DailyMed) in place of the DrugCentral copy of the Hikma label; added extended-release antacid spacing (Teva ER label), live oral typhoid vaccine (Vivotif label), intravesical BCG (TICE BCG label) and fecal microbiota spores (Vowst label), each verified verbatim on openFDA. Not added: neomycin/nephrotoxic drugs (no US cefaclor label lists them).
